title: The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life Anime Gets Same-Day English Dub
content:
The English dub stars:

• Justin Briner as Rein

• Hollis Beck as Lily

• Lacey Deline as Nina

• KyLeigh Zimmerer as Elsie

• Rick Robertson as Barrius

The dub staff includes:

• Studio: Crunchyroll

• Studio Producers: Justin Cook, Michael Harcourt, Nathanael Harrison

• Producer: Susie Nixon

• Adaptation Supervisor: Tyler Walker

• Adaptation: Clayton Browning

• Adaptation Prep: Marilyn M. Reyes, Benjamin Tehrani

• Voice Director: Jerry Jewell

• Talent Coordination: Tara A. Williams, Brittni Hurley

• Engineering Managers: Gino Palencia, Brandon Peters

• Engineer: Sawyer Pfledderer

• Mixer: Andrew Tipps

The anime will premiere on TV Tokyo and its affiliates on Tuesday at 24:00 (effectively, Wednesday at midnight), and on AT-X on Thursday. Crunchyroll will stream the anime as it airs in Japan.

Shochiku describes the anime:

Rein, an enchanter who strengthens equipment with his magic, is suddenly expelled from his guild, simply because every piece of gear in the guild has already been enhanced enough. Outraged by the absurd treatment, Rein decides to take back the enormous amount of mana he had poured into their equipment. When he casually channels it into a random copper sword, it transforms into a cheat-level weapon with 10,000 enhancement points! With zero combat experience but armed with magic that can turn anything into overpowered gear, this enchanter sets off to enjoy a new, carefree life as an adventurer! In a world where magic and science intertwine, wild humor meets layered character drama, fueling nonstop fan theories and generating major buzz long before the anime was even announced.

Shū Honma ( Ya Boy Kongming! , Mayonaka Punch , Tatsuki Fujimoto 17-26 "Sisters") is directing the anime at P.A. Works . Yōko Yonaiyama ( Botan Kamiina Fully Blossoms When Drunk , mono, Ya Boy Kongming! ) is in charge of the series scripts. Tadahito Kiyosawa is designing the characters, with Masami Gohda as the sub-character designer. Both Kiyosawa and Gohda also serve as chief animation directors.

Rokushima began serializing the original story in the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in January 2021, and is still updating the story. Kodansha published the first print volume of the novels with illustrations by kisui in January 2022, and the second volume shipped in October 2022.

Gyōmuyōmochi launched the manga adaptation in Kodansha 's Shōnen Magazine R in November 2021, and moved the manga to Kodansha 's Comic Days app in March 2023 after Shōnen Magazine R ended publication. Kodansha released the manga's 21st compiled book volume on August 7. Kodansha 's K MANGA service is releasing the manga digitally in English.

title: Demon Slayer Studio’s Next Big Movie Shows Off Surprise Crossover
content:
The studio behind Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba has a new movie on the way, and it’s gearing up for its debut with a cool crossover with another of Ufotable’s biggest franchises. Fans might be anxiously waiting to find out new updates on the next film in the Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle trilogy, but studio Ufotable has been keeping quite busy with other projects in the meantime. That includes another feature film that’s slated to make its way through theaters in Japan later this Fall.

Witch on the Holy Night is the next major feature film release coming from Studio Ufotable after they had been working on other TYPE-MOON franchise releases in the past such as various anime in the Fate series. Now with the newest film bringing TYPE-MOON back to the big screen with Studio Ufotable , the two franchises have united in a cool crossover to get fans ready for the new movie. Check it out below.

Witch on the Holy Night x Fate/Zero Crossover Revealed

To help celebrate the upcoming debut of Witch on the Holy Night in Japan , TYPE-MOON and Ufotable have kicked off a “Let’s all watch it together! TYPE-MOON × ufotable” special crossover project for both franchises. This will include a special broadcast of certain films from Ufotable’s TYPE-MOON adaptations in the region, but also this special crossover visual with Fate/Zero. With the classic series also celebrating its 15th anniversary in Japan as of this month, it’s a big event for fans in quite a few ways with that classic series getting more love after all this time.

Witch on the Holy Night will be making its debut in Japan on November 20th, so it won’t be too much longer before fans get to see it all in action. Making matters even more enticing is the fact that the film has also confirmed it will be coming to international territories in 2027. Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment will be bringing the new film to the United States, Canada and more international territories on January 29th next year , but there could be even more updates about it by the end of the year.

What to Know for Witch on the Holy Night

Witch on the Holy Night is directed by Masashi Takeuchi for ufotable with Moe Tsuzuki providing the character designs, Manabu Kamino handling the editing, and Hideyuki Fukasawa composing the music. The Japanese cast will be reprising their respective roles from the original TYPE-MOON visual novel too with the likes of Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki, Kana Hanazawa as Alice Kuonji, and Yusuke Kobayashi as Soujyuro Sizuki confirmed thus far. But any potential English dub cast members have yet to be announced as of this time.

The film will be releasing in the United States with both Japanese and Engliah language audio, but we will likely see more updates for it revealed in the coming months. This crossover further emphasizes just how many similarities that the TYPE-MOON franchises have with one another, and Ufotable has been able to elevate that even more for their respective anime outings over the years. But how are you liking the way Witch on the Holy Night looks so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: MediaOCD Announces Deal to Sell Physical Editions of Manga from Manga Mavericks Books, Mahjong Pros
content:
Manga currently available on MediaOCD 's website from Manga Mavericks Books include ALTERNATIVE[SELF LINER NOTE], First Time in Taiwan: A Delicious Adventure, FISHGOD, Great Metal God , Horon of the Closed Country , Princess Da Huang & Other Tales, The Pipe Machine , Vegetable Sandwich , and Zigoku's Foreman .

The Manga Mavericks website and podcast established the Manga Mavericks Books publishing division in April 2025 to license, localize, and distribute works worldwide from indie creators in Japan.

Manga Mavericks announced in July the Independent Manga Alliance, an industry association and joint venture between Manga Mavericks CEO Varun Gupta and Mahjong Pros head of partnerships and licensing Harrison Doan . The venture aims to provide distribution, marketing, and sales support to independent creators and small publishers, linking them to partner publishers and distributors located in the United States or globally. The founding members of the Independent Manga Alliance are Manga Mavericks Books , Mahjong Pros , Strict Algorithm LLC , Red String Manga, and Curation Entertainment Partners Inc.

Manga Mavericks Books entered a distribution deal with Pathway Book Service and with Gazelle Book Services Ltd for Europe last February. Pathway is handling comprehensive book fulfillment, warehousing, and retail distribution for Manga Mavericks Books .

Mahjong set company Mahjong Pros ' Mahjong Pros Publishing imprint focuses on licensing, localizing, and distributing mahjong-themed manga and textbooks. The company announced its Mahjong Pros Publishing imprint in June 2025.

title: Hunter x Hunter Creator Shares New Health Update Amidst Shonen Jump Hiatus
content:
Hunter x Hunter is back on hiatus from the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, and the creator behind it all has shared a new update on changes to their schedule. Yoshihiro Togashi began Hunter x Hunter decades ago , but the series unfortunately has gone on hiatus multiple times through the course of its serialization. Some of these hiatuses have lasted for years at a time as the creator’s poor health unfortunately makes it difficult to maintain a steadier release schedule for the chapters. But Togashi has made great strides in the past few years.

Togashi has been returning to Shonen Jump in the 2020s with more steady chapter releases with only a couple of years of hiatus in between. Returning for ten new chapters earlier this Summer before going on hiatus once more , the creator took to social media to announce even more changes to his production schedule as he notes that he’s no longer taking on any work that requires to be turned in under a deadline at this time.

Hunter x Hunter Creator Shares New Production Update Amid Shonen Jump Hiatus

As Togashi noted to fans on social media, “Due to a combination of physical and mental health issues, I’ve decided that after completing the work I’m currently committed to, I will turn down all future requests that come with deadlines and prioritize working on my own manuscripts,” the creator stated. “Once I’m able to resume work on them, I’ll announce it on Twitter.” It seems that while working on new chapters of Hunter x Hunter, the creator had been working on other tasks and keeping up with deadlines. But it seems like his health has made it to where he can only work on the coming chapters of his own manuscripts instead .

Hunter x Hunter recently went back on hiatus after resuming for ten new chapters earlier this year . This was following a two year hiatus where the creator previously returned to Shonen Jump for a slate of ten chapters as well. This seems to be the pattern for Togashi and Shueisha’s editors at this time. The creator returns every couple of years for a physical volume’s worth of chapters, and it means we’ll eventually get to the end of the Succession Contest Arc in the coming years.

What Does This Mean for Hunter x Hunter?

Hunter x Hunter has gone on hiatus following the release of Chapter 420 of the manga, and Togashi is already hard at work on the next ten chapters of the series. If he continues at the same pace as before, it’s likely going to be a 2028 release window for the chapters. With the Succession Contest Arc now at its climax , it also means that the Dark Continent is closer than ever before. But there are so many characters now in the mix in the latest chapters, it’s hard to gauge where it’s all going.

Hunter x Hunter fans have been anxious to see many of their favorites in action, and that unfortunately has been one of the most stinging aspects of each of these hiatuses. Gon and Killua finally made a cameo appearance in the manga’s pages after nearly 15 long years, and that just made the waiting all the more intense. But how are you feeling about Hunter x Hunter right now? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Confirms U.S. Release Date & New Streaming Platform
content:
Dragon Ball Super is coming our way with a new remake anime series offering an enhanced version of the original TV series, and it has expanded its streaming offerings with a new United States release date update. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is an new take on the now classic TV anime series that’s going all the way back to the Battle of Gods arc, and it’s going to be one of the big releases fans can’t wait to check out this October . Now it’s gotten a whole new streaming platform ahead of its release.

Crunchyroll has officially announced that they will be streaming Dragon Ball Super: Beerus alongside its release in Japan on October 11th. This is following the reveal that Netflix would also be offering the series some time after on October 17th. This makes its release with Crunchyroll the first one that fans should look into if they want to check out the remake as soon as the new episodes hit. It’s time to mark your calendars for the big debut.

Dragon Ball Super Remake Confirms Crunchyroll Streaming Release Date

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will be making its debut on October 11th in Japan , and will be streaming its new episodes with Crunchyroll for fans in the United States, Canada, Latin America including Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, Southeast Asia and Europe. It will then be followed by a streaming release with Netflix a week later on October 17th. Both streaming services will be offering the remake with Japanese language audio and English subtitles, but any potential English dub release plans have yet to be announced as of this time.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will be an “enhanced” edition of the original TV anime series teased by Toei to feature “extensive new cuts, revisions to existing scenes, a complete re-rendering of all footage, newly recorded dubbing with added score and sound effects, and a full reconstruction of the story. ” The extent of the changes have yet to be revealed as of this time, but will be far more clear once the anime starts to kick off its remake run in full later this month.

What to Know for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will be directed by Tadayoshi Yamamuro for Toei Animation with Matsuto Seya providing the composition and direction arrangement, Eichi Nishimura serving as editor, Yosuke Motoki serving as compositing director, and Norihito Sumitomo composing the music. The new remake series is also getting an update set of opening and ending themes for the occasion too. The new opening theme is titled “ONOGAMI” as performed by MEGATERA・ZERO, and a new ending theme titled “Kan Peki No Peki” as performed by VK Blanka.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will be adapting the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F, and Universe 6 arcs from the original TV anime series, but it’s yet to be revealed whether or not fans will see the other arcs get their own remakes as of this time. It’s also yet to be confirmed how many episodes this new series will have on offer either , so there’s lots to look forward to either way. Are you excited to check out Dragon Ball Super ‘s remake this Fall? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Crunchyroll to Stream Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Anime Starting on October 11
content:
Crunchyroll announced on Monday that it will simultaneously stream the Dragon Ball Super: Beerus television anime series in Japanese with English subtitles on October 11 in the United States, Canada, Latin America including Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, Southeast Asia, and Europe.

The series will begin airing on the Fuji TV channel and its affiliates on October 11 at 11:15 p.m. JST (10:15 a.m. EDT), taking over the timeslot of the One Piece anime, which aired its last episode for this year on September 27. The series will also stream on Amazon Prime Video and U-NEXT streaming services in Japan 30 minutes after its broadcast at 12:15 a.m. JST.

Netflix will also stream the series in the U.S. on October 17, and is listed to start streaming on October 14 in selected areas/countries.

The first episode will also screen in advance at the Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Special Panel at New York Comic Con on October 8.

The staff for the new anime includes:

• Composition and Direction Arrangement: Matsuto Seya

• Animation Character Design & General Animation Director: Tadayoshi Yamamuro

• Editing: Eiichi Nishimura

• Compositing Director: Yōsuke Motoki

• Music: Norihito Sumitomo

The anime will again feature Kōichi Yamadera as Beerus.

MEGATERA･ZERO performs the opening theme song "ONOGAMI," and VK Blanka performs the ending theme song "Kan Peki No Peki."

Akio Iyoku stated the work started a few years ago and is an "enhanced" edition of the Dragon Ball Super anime that features a reconstruction of the story, and includes new and redrawn cuts.

The official announcement of the anime stated:

The project features extensive new cuts, revisions to existing scenes, a complete re-rendering of all footage, newly recorded dubbing with added score and sound effects, and a full reconstruction of the story. Living up to the name ENHANCED, this edition employs the latest visual expression to deliver greater power and immersion across all scenes, especially the battle sequences. The result is an ENHANCED edition that expresses Akira Toriyama 's original idea and worldbuilding more accurately, that will be broadcasted with highly satisfying quality.

The anime staff stated, "the anime Dragon Ball Super ... is set to begin anew as Dragon Ball Super: Beerus in Fall 2026."

The staff describes the story:

Several years have passed since the fierce battle against Majin Buu, and Earth has finally regained a brief moment of peace. At the same time, Beerus, the God of Destruction, awakens from his long, deep sleep. Even Kai and Supreme Kai, aware of Beerus's overwhelming power to destroy entire planets, watch his awakening with great fear… Meanwhile, Beerus hears rumors of a Saiyan who defeated Frieza—and suddenly appears before Goku.Targeted by Beerus, the strongest being in the universe, Earth is in grave danger. Thus begins an Earth-shattering cosmic battle between the God of Destruction and Goku and his allies—a conflict that will shake the entire universe.

Dragon Ball Super premiered in July 2015 and aired for 131 episodes until March 2018. Funimation and Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired, and Funimation released the series on home video. Funimation debuted the English dub to its streaming service in December 2016. The English dub premiered on Adult Swim 's Toonami block in January 2017.

The anime staff stated, "the anime Dragon Ball Super ... is set to begin anew as Dragon Ball Super: Beerus in Fall 2026."
The staff describes the story:

Several years have passed since the fierce battle against Majin Buu, and Earth has finally regained a brief moment of peace. At the same time, Beerus, the God of Destruction, awakens from his long, deep sleep. Even Kai and Supreme Kai, aware of Beerus's overwhelming power to destroy entire planets, watch his awakening with great fear… Meanwhile, Beerus hears rumors of a Saiyan who defeated Frieza—and suddenly appears before Goku.Targeted by Beerus, the strongest being in the universe, Earth is in grave danger. Thus begins an Earth-shattering cosmic battle between the God of Destruction and Goku and his allies—a conflict that will shake the entire universe.

Dragon Ball Super premiered in July 2015 and aired for 131 episodes until March 2018. Funimation and Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired, and Funimation released the series on home video. Funimation debuted the English dub to its streaming service in December 2016. The English dub premiered on Adult Swim 's Toonami block in January 2017.

title: Crunchyroll Just Removed Fan-Favorite Anime Series & You Can’t Stream It Anywhere Else
content:
A fan-favorite anime series has just been removed from Crunchyroll, and now fans can’t find it streaming anywhere else after this latest update. Crunchyroll is one of the biggest anime streaming platforms out there as they just launched a new wave of releases as part of the Fall 2026 anime schedule . While there are going to be plenty of new titles to keep an eye out for over the next few months, unfortunately it seems like some of the classic shows are no longer available to stream with the platform.

The anime adaptation for Takahiro and Tetsuya Tashiro’s Akame ga Kill! is one such series. It’s a big fan-favorite among classic anime watchers as it introduces a main cast that’s not safe from harm by any means, and its complete story makes it a great watch to check out. But now that’s even tougher as not only has Akame ga Kill! previously been removed from platforms like HIDIVE, Prime Video and Netflix through the year thus far , it’s now been taken down from its last streaming home, Crunchyroll.

Akame ga Kill! Is Removed From Crunchyroll

Now that Akame ga Kill! has disappeared from Crunchyroll, it’s now no longer available for streaming in the United States on any viable platform. It’s a shame because the classic anime series has remained a part of the conversation even 12 years after it came to an end. It’s an action series with a ton of consequence for each of the characters, and the surprise in how it accomplishes all of this is why fans still hold it in high regard to this day. It was often recommended as an early watch for fans just getting into anime for how quickly you can make it through its complete tale .

It’s also a series that packs a lot of surprise into its 24 episode run, and that’s especially true for all of the characters involved . There are a lot of favorites that come and go through the series relatively quickly, and it’s easy to get attached. But it’s even easier to get your heartbroken when you have to say goodbye to many of them. Part of the fun is checking it all out for the first time, and unfortunately this update makes it much harder to do so unless you have access to one of its rare physical releases.

What Does This Mean for Crunchyroll?

Crunchyroll’s removal of Akame ga Kill! is likely for the same reason as other streaming platforms before it. This is just another case of a license for a classic series ending, and there’s always a chance it can be brought back to the streaming service (or any other platform) in the future. That’s happened before with a few other titles, but unfortunately the other side of that has been just as true. There have been shows that disappeared from the platform, and have yet to make their return even years after their removal .

This latest removal is unfortunately yet another classic anime series that has had its license expire with Crunchyroll through the year thus far , but hopefully it has a better chance of returning given how big it has been with fans in the decade since its original launch. Are you hoping to see Akame ga Kill ! return to streaming soon? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Magical Explorer TV Anime Confirms English Dub Cast
content:
• Alex Mai as Kosuke

• Kayla Temshiv as Ludivine

• Gerard Caster as Aurelien

• Krystal LaPorte as Claris

• Madeleine Norton as Marino

• Ezra Vervin as Hatsumi

The dub staff includes:

• Studio: Crunchyroll

• Studio Producers: Justin Cook, Michael Harcourt, Nathanael Harrison

• Producer: Samantha Herek

• Adaptation Supervisor: Ben Phillips

• Adaptation: Blair Rowan

• Adaptation Prep: Benjamin Tehrani

• Voice Director: Helena Walstrom

• Assistant Voice Director: Kevin D. Thelwell

• Talent Coordination: Tara A. Williams, Brittni Hurley

• Engineering Managers: Gino Palencia, Brandon Peters

• Engineer: Noah Whitehead

• Mixer: Andrew Tipps

The series debuted with two episodes on October 3 at 24:00 (effectively October 4 at 12:00 a.m.) on Tokyo MX , Tochigi TV , Gunma TV , and BS11 . The anime also airs on Tohoku Broadcasting, TV Aichi , and YTV .

Kazuki Ohashi ( Shadows House ) is directing the anime at WHITE FOX . Satoko Sekine ( TsukiPro the Animation ) is handling series composition. Ryosuke Kimiya ( Grimoire of Zero ) is designing the characters. Kenichiro Suehiro ( Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- ) is composing the music.

ASCA performs the show's opening theme song "Remedy" and the ending theme song "Double Wings."

Additional staff members include:

• Prop Design: Yaeko Watanabe, Yūkei Yamada

• Monster Design: Naoto Hosoda

• Effect Design: Hiroshi Yakou

• Art Director: Yūki Yokoyama

• Color Design: Eriko Murata

• Director of Photography: Shinya Kuwabara

• 3D Director: Haruka Sakaguchi

• Special Effects and 2D Works: Keiko Ōnishi

• Editing: Masahiro Gotō

• Sound Director: Jin Aketagawa

• Sound Effects: Toshiya Wada

• Executive Producer: Gaku Iwasa

• Animation Producer: Shin'ichirō Katō

Yen Press is publishing the light novel series and Yukari Higa 's manga adaptation, and it describes the story:

Living in the world of Magical★Explorer, the legendary erotic game, sounds like a dream. Problem is, I reincarnated not as the lady-killer protagonist with his overpowered cheat skills, but as his unlucky comic-relief best friend!

The novel series debuted in February 2018 on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website. Kadokawa began publishing the light novel series in November 2019. The 14th volume shipped on October 1.

The manga adaptation launched in Young Ace Up in August 2020. Kadokawa published the manga's fourth compiled book volume on October 2.

title: Black Clover Season 2 Preview Reveals First Look at Big Transformations
content:
Black Clover has finally made its return to screens with its highly anticipated second season, and the anime is showing off the first look at some big transformations with the preview for its next episode. Black Clover Season 2 is now airing its episodes as part of the Fall 2026 anime schedule, and with it fans have been thrown right back into the conflict. Asta and the others have been readying for a raid on the Spade Kingdom, and it’s time for these rematches to kick off in full.

Black Clover Season 2’s premiere saw the Magic Knights making their way into the Spade Kingdom to face off against the members of the Dark Triad , and now it’s time for those fights to actually kick in as the Magic Knights reveal the fruits of their few days of training for this exact moment. And the first look at Black Clover Season 2 Episode 2 actually shows these new power ups off for the first time. Check out the images in the gallery below.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 2 Confirms Release Date & Synopsis

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 2 is titled “The Gate to Hell” and will be making its debut in Japan on October 10th, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it hits for fans in North America and other international territories. The synopsis for the episode teases the showdowns that had been seen in the first episode too as “Charlotte confronts Vanica, who harbors the demon Megicula, the source of the curse, while Yuno faces Zenon, who kidnapped Vangeance right before his eyes.”

As for the other conflicts, Black Clover teases that the episode will then see, “Jack and Nacht, though struggling, are fighting on equal footing with Dante, who wields the strongest physical magic.” But as teased by one of the preview images, it won’t just be the Dark Triad that needs to be dealt with as a mysterious pair of new Devils will be making their debut in the episode too. Which means that the series will be gearing up for an even bigger crisis long before Asta even makes his way to the scene.

What’s Next for Black Clover Season 2?

Black Clover Season 2 won’t be around for nearly as long as the first season did, and that’s even more evident after the premiere episode . The Spade Kingdom Raid arc chapters from Yuki Tabata’s original manga really aren’t that long, and when accounting for the chapters that are pretty much all fight scenes, it seems like the new season is going to be adapting the chapters at a steady clip. The premiere takes on a little under five chapters, and this preview teases the second episode is going to do the same.

The twins showing up here teases about another four or so chapters covered within this second episode, and that pace further teases that Black Clover Season 2 might only be lasting for a single cour of episodes for the Fall. The anime has yet to confirm its episode order for its return, so it’s something to keep an eye out for as the series continues to work towards Asta’s big fights to come . What are you hoping to see in Black Clover ‘s next Season 2 episode? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Naruto’s Live-Action Movie Has Way Bigger Plans Than You Think
content:
A new report is teasing that if the new Naruto live-action movie ends up being a success, there could be way more movies planned than any fan could have ever expected. Masashi Kishimoto’s Naruto recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and with it has made a return with all kinds of new projects. Not only are fans going to be treated to a full revival of the classic anime series , but there’s also a live-action feature film adaptation that’s set to go into full production in the near future.

Naruto has kicked off a global casting search for its new live-action feature film debut , and new details about the project have been steadily making their way online through multiple reports. It’s yet to be revealed if any of these reports will pan out, but one of the most curious comes from notable leaker Daniel RPK as the report notes that there could end up being “7-8 films overall” by the time the live-action Naruto franchise wraps up if everything goes well.

Naruto Could Get 8 Live-Action Movies Like Harry Potter

As fans know too well (and have criticized the anime about for decades), Naruto is a very long series. It comes from the earlier eras of Shueisha’s Shonen Jump magazine where creators were encouraged to keep their stories going for a long time, and Naruto spans multiple eras, arcs, and even has two major halves to its story following a time skip. Adapting such a massive story would be an ordeal , which is why the report notes that the plan for the franchise is to follow the Harry Potter model and working it out over seven or eight films.

“Part 1” of the original series would be a trilogy of films, and then the events of Naruto: Shippuden would then wrap up the second half with three or four films. The early story reports for this debut film teases an adaptation of the Land of Waves arc, which would be a suitable start to the entire film franchise . But if there’s a success, then it does raise a lot of questions about not only how long it would take to adapt the story but whether or not something of that nature is even possible.

Will Naruto’s Live-Action Movie Even Work?

This report does feel a bit like it’s putting the cart before the horse for now as the first film hasn’t even started production. This eight film projection is clearly just an early plan for the best possible outcome, but that’s not exactly feasible within the current Hollywood feature film market. Director Destin Daniel Cretton is taking on the film, but is in such high demand that he’s likely going to return to the Spider-Man franchise (or some other notable project ) after Naruto wraps up its production. It’d make an even longer wait for a sequel, let along eight different films.

That’s also not factoring in any potential changes to Naruto ‘s original story. Reports of potential character alterations are already making fans upset, and this is all before any big changes to its story are made. There could be eight different films, but it would be even more realistic to shoot for a trilogy that has a complete story and ending. This live-action version is going to be different than fans will expect, so don’t really hold out hope for a long film franchise either. It’s going to be altered to make it more streamlined for this new version of the story.

How many live-action Naruto films would you want to see? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

HT – Daniel RPK
